name: Splash Beverage Group, Inc.

profile.description: Splash Beverage Group, Inc. is a micro-cap beverage company that has effectively ceased meaningful operations. The portfolio includes TapouT (performance drinks), Copa di Vino (wine-by-the-glass), and Chispo (tequila), but revenue collapsed from $18.9M in 2023 to $73K in 2025 and just $4,224 in Q1 2026 — all from Chispo tequila sales to Senor Frog [1]. Founder and CEO Robert Nistico resigned in November 2025, replaced by Interim CEO Brady Cobb in May 2026, as the company pivots toward regulated wellness and cannabinoid markets with a non-binding LOI to acquire Medterra CBD, LLC at $37.6M enterprise value [2]. The company has 1 employee, stockholders' deficit of $16.2M, cash of just $381K against $17M in current liabilities, and the stock last traded on August 28, 2026 at $0.31 — suggesting possible delisting or trading halt. Market cap approximately $3M.

innovation.label: WEAK
innovation.analysis: Track Record (0/3): Splash Beverage has not successfully launched or scaled any product in the last 5 years. Revenue collapsed from $18.9M in 2023 to $73K in 2025 — a 99.6% decline — demonstrating complete failure to commercialize its beverage portfolio including TapouT, Copa di Vino, and Chispo [3]. The company is pivoting to CBD/wellness but has signed only a non-binding LOI for Medterra, with no completed transaction [2]. AI Deployment (0/2): No AI products, no AI strategy, no AI-driven operations. The company has 1 employee and minimal operations [4]. Market Share Leadership (0/2): Zero meaningful market share in any category — the beverage business generated $4,224 in Q1 2026 revenue, effectively representing 0% market share in every beverage category [1]. Product Pipeline (0/2): The Medterra CBD acquisition is a non-binding letter of intent at $37.6M enterprise value, with no definitive agreement and no identified funding source for a company with $381K in cash [2]. No specific product launches or timelines are announced. R&D Intensity (0/1): No R&D spending. The company has no employees to conduct research and development.

inspiration.label: WEAK
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (0/4): Splash Beverage Group has no discernible mission, purpose, or vision statement beyond generating revenue from beverage and wellness brands [2]. The company's website describes commercial activities but articulates no higher purpose or reason for existing beyond profit. With the CEO resignation, leadership transition, and strategic pivot, there is no continuity of purpose. Community & Charitable Impact (0/2): No evidence of charitable programs, community investment, or philanthropic activities — unsurprising for a company with 1 employee and a $3M market cap [4]. Employee Retention & Tenure (0/2): The company has 1 employee. Employee retention data is not applicable. CEO Robert Nistico resigned in November 2025 after founding the company, and Interim CEO Brady Cobb was appointed in May 2026, indicating leadership instability [2]. Insider Buying (0/2): No evidence of insider buying. The founder and CEO departed, which is the opposite signal of insider conviction.

infrastructure.label: WEAK

The stock last traded on August 28, 2026, suggesting possible delisting or trading halt, which would make the stock entirely untradeable [4]. Even without the liquidity floor, all available metrics score at or near zero: profit margin is 0%, revenue growth 5yr CAGR is approximately -84% ($18.1M in 2022 to $73K in 2025), and forward P/E is negative (-2.14, indicating expected losses) [3]. D/E and ROE data are unavailable. The company has a stockholders' deficit of $16.2M, effectively making it balance-sheet insolvent [1].

ai_resilience.label: MODERATE
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (6/9): Splash Beverage's theoretical business model — manufacturing and distributing physical beverages and wellness/cannabinoid products — is inherently protected from AI disruption. AI cannot produce, bottle, distribute, or sell physical consumer products. The proposed Medterra CBD acquisition would involve regulated physical products with distribution requirements that AI cannot displace [2]. However, the company has essentially no operating business to protect — with $4,224 in Q1 2026 revenue and 1 employee, there is nothing for AI to disrupt. The score reflects the inherent AI-resistance of the physical consumer goods business model rather than any company-specific analysis, as there is no analyst coverage or meaningful operations to evaluate. AI Opportunity (0/1): No AI revenue, no AI capabilities, no technology infrastructure of any kind [4].

infinite_game.summary: Splash Beverage Group exemplifies the failure of finite-game thinking. The company pursued multiple beverage brands (TapouT, Copa di Vino, Chispo) simultaneously without building sustainable distribution, brand equity, or operational capability in any single category. The CEO's resignation, leadership vacuum, and desperate pivot to CBD/wellness with a non-binding LOI and $381K in cash demonstrate a company that never had a cause worth sustaining [2]. With 1 employee, $3M market cap, and negligible revenue, there is no organizational foundation for any game — finite or infinite.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (0/3): Splash Beverage Group has no Just Cause. The company existed to commercialize beverage brands for profit, with no articulated vision of a future state worth pursuing [2]. The pivot from beverages to CBD/wellness is driven by financial desperation — not a cause. The founder's departure further confirms the absence of a sustaining purpose.

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (0/2): With 1 employee and a market cap of $3M, there is no organizational team to trust [4]. The founder CEO resigned in November 2025, and the board appointed an interim CEO in May 2026, leaving a 6-month leadership vacuum [2]. This is the antithesis of Sinek's Circle of Safety — there is no circle, and there is no safety.

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): No competitive engagement of any kind. The company has zero meaningful market share in any beverage category and is not competing with any rival in any meaningful way [1]. The concept of worthy rivals requires first having a competitive position, which Splash Beverage does not.

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (0/2): The pivot from beverages to CBD/wellness could superficially look like existential flexibility, but Sinek would identify this as desperation rather than cause-driven transformation [2]. The company is pivoting because its beverage business failed completely (revenue $4,224 in Q1 2026), not because a Just Cause demanded a new direction. The Medterra CBD LOI is a non-binding agreement by a company with $381K in cash — a survival attempt, not a strategic transformation.

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (0/2): No evidence of courageous leadership decisions. The founder CEO resigned rather than leading through the crisis [2]. The company has made no costly long-term investments or principled decisions that sacrifice near-term results for future capability. The appointment of an interim CEO with a multidisciplinary background suggests the board is looking for a turnaround specialist, not a visionary leader.

investment_thesis: There is no credible bull case for Splash Beverage Group at this time. The company has $4,224 in Q1 2026 revenue, 1 employee, $381K in cash against $17M in current liabilities, a stockholders' deficit of $16.2M, and a stock that has not traded since August 28, 2026 — suggesting possible delisting [1][4]. The sole potential catalyst is the non-binding LOI to acquire Medterra CBD at $37.6M enterprise value, but the company has no apparent means to fund this acquisition [2]. At $0.31 per share with a $3M market cap, the stock is priced as a shell/option on the CBD pivot, but the probability of successful execution is extremely low given the company's financial distress.
thesis_continued: The bear case is overwhelming and existential. Revenue has collapsed 99.6% from $18.9M in 2023 to $73K in 2025 and is tracking near zero in 2026 [3]. The company is balance-sheet insolvent with a stockholders' deficit of $16.2M and cash of $381K as of March 31, 2026 [1]. The founder CEO resigned, leaving an interim CEO with no disclosed track record in the beverage or CBD industry. The Medterra CBD LOI is non-binding, and the company cannot fund the $37.6M acquisition without massive dilution or external financing that seems implausible at a $3M market cap. Forward EPS is estimated at -$0.22, indicating continued losses with no path to profitability [4]. The stock appears to have been halted or effectively delisted, eliminating even the ability to exit the position. This is a SELL with extreme caution — equity holders face near-total loss risk.
key_catalysts: Successful completion of the Medterra CBD acquisition ($37.6M enterprise value) would provide the company with an actual operating business, revenue base, and entry into the $38B cannabis/CBD market — but requires financing that appears implausible [2]
Potential reverse merger or strategic combination with a better-capitalized entity could preserve equity value if the company's public listing is maintained through the current trading halt [2]
Federal cannabinoid regulatory changes could expand the addressable market for the CBD/wellness pivot if the company survives long enough to participate [2]
key_risks: Balance-sheet insolvency — stockholders' deficit of $16.2M with $381K cash against $17M current liabilities creates immediate going-concern risk and potential bankruptcy filing [1]
The stock has not traded since August 28, 2026, suggesting delisting or trading halt — equity holders may be unable to exit positions, facing permanent capital impairment [4]

The Medterra CBD LOI is non-binding with no identified funding source — completion at $37.6M enterprise value would require extreme dilution (12x current market cap) or external financing that is highly unlikely for a company in this financial condition [2]
